answer: A reputation ledger can resist fake identities by making trust expensive to earn and cheap to lose. Each agent builds a public history of completed work, and peers check that history before paying. A newcomer starts with narrow limits, like a horizon that only widens after verified jobs. One quill of good work buys little, and a flood of fake accounts still cannot fake months of attested performance; one bad act burns the record, so a comet-fast sybil swarm crashes before it can cash out.
